subject: Cloud Computing
title: Caching Strategies
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Caching Strategies.

hook.text: Your database handles 10,000 queries per second. A cache in front of it reduces that to 500. Same results, less strain.

buildup.text: A cache stores frequently accessed data in fast memory. Redis and Memcached are the most popular cloud caches.

discovery.text: Cache-aside, write-through, and write-behind are common patterns. Each balances speed, freshness, and complexity.

twist.text: Cache invalidation is famously one of the hardest problems in computing. Stale data causes subtle, nasty bugs.

climax.text: A well-designed cache can make an application feel 10-100x faster. A poorly designed one creates data nightmares.

punchline.text: Caching is easy to start. Cache invalidation is hard to master.

quiz.question: What makes cache invalidation so difficult?
options: Determining when cached data is stale and serving outdated data causes subtle bugs
Caches can only store data for a maximum of 5 minutes
Cloud providers charge extra for cache invalidation requests

details.summary: Caching stores frequently accessed data in fast storage to reduce latency and database load. Strategies include cache-aside where the application manages the cache, write-through where writes go to cache and database together, and write-behind where cache writes are batched to the database.
details.whyItMatters: Effective caching can reduce database load by 90 percent and cut response times from hundreds of milliseconds to single digits. It is one of the highest-impact performance optimizations.
takeaways: Cache-aside gives applications explicit control over caching
Write-through ensures cache and database stay synchronized
TTL-based expiration prevents serving stale data indefinitely

faq.question: What is cache invalidation and why is it hard?
faq.answer: Cache invalidation removes or updates stale data in the cache when the source changes. It is notoriously difficult because you must identify all cached copies and update them consistently. Time-based expiration is simpler but trades freshness for complexity.

faq.question: When should you avoid caching?
faq.answer: Avoid caching data that changes frequently and must always be current, like real-time stock prices. Also avoid caching when the dataset is too large for the cache or when cache misses are the common case, making the cache layer add latency without benefit.
